System-Message Unread Badge Fix — Full 4-Cell Verification

Skill: test-on-device — Android emulator (WEIF_API_36) on host loopback (10.0.2.2:8080)
Backend: cd server && DEV_LOGIN_ENABLED=1 go run .
Test users: Tester (id=5), Host (id=6), Member2 (id=7) — signed in via the __DEV__-gated DevLoginButton

Final verdict: PASS — No red unread dot appears in any of the 4 cells (Group × {Host, Member} and 1:1 × {Host, Member}) when the conversation's last message is a system message ("X joined the chat", "Updated Event Detail"). Real user messages still badge correctly (regression guard confirmed across all POVs).

4. Regression guard — real user messages still badge

Across every POV, a real kind='user' message correctly bumps unread_count to 1 and shows the red UnreadDot:

// DB row proving kind='user' is still counted:
id 18, sender_id=6, body='Hey Tester, see you there!', kind='user'

// countUnreadMessages for tester (id=5):
SELECT COUNT(1) FROM messages WHERE conversation_id=8
  AND id > COALESCE((SELECT last_read_message_id FROM conversation_read_state WHERE conversation_id=8 AND user_id=5), 0)
  AND sender_id <> 5
  AND kind <> 'system';
→ 1   (the kind='user' message is correctly counted; system messages are excluded)

5. System messages render inline in the chat thread

System messages are NOT hidden — they appear inline in the chat thread (and as the last-message preview), so members still see the activity. The fix only suppresses the unread badge, not the message itself.

6. The fix (recap)

  • Schema: messages.kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user' column added; ensureMessageKindColumn migration backfills existing system rows (body = 'Updated Event Detail' or body LIKE '% joined the chat').
  • Server models: MessageKind constants ('user' | 'system'); Kind field on Message, MessageSummary, CreateMessageParams; messagePayload.Kind in the WS envelope.
  • Server-tagged producers: postJoinAnnouncement ("X joined the chat") and emitEventUpdateChatMessages ("Updated Event Detail") both pass Kind: MessageKindSystem; handleSend (user-typed message) passes MessageKindUser; approveSingleJoinRequest's intro message is explicitly tagged MessageKindUser.
  • Server-side unread exclusion (the long-term fix that survives refresh): countUnreadMessages query is WHERE conversation_id = ? AND id > ? AND sender_id <> ? AND kind <> 'system'.
  • Client types + live WS exclusion: ChatMessage.kind; the message:new handler skips unreadCount++ when message.kind === 'system' (defense in depth alongside the server-side exclusion).
  • Tiebreaker: selectLatestMessageForConversation now uses ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC so when multiple messages share a timestamp the most-recently-inserted wins deterministically (was a source of test flakiness when approve + edit landed in the same second).

8. Why no inconsistencies remain

  • Single source of truth: the kind column on the messages row is the one fact every consumer reads — live WS, REST /api/conversations, REST /api/conversations/:id/messages, push, future system-message rendering.
  • Server-side exclusion means the badge can't reappear after refreshConversations — the previous inconsistency source (client WS handler alone) is gone.
  • Both group and 1:1 flow through the identical path: emitEventUpdateChatMessages iterates PostMigrationConversationIDs = SELECT id FROM conversations WHERE event_id = ? (returns the group convo for Group events and every approved host↔requester private convo for 1:1 events). The kind tag and unread exclusion apply identically to all of them.
  • Both host and member perspectives verified end-to-end on the emulator — no dot in any of the 4 cells; regression guard (real user message → dot appears) confirmed for Tester on the old Emulator Test Group Event.
  • Migration backfills existing system rows, so already-badged conversations clear on the next /api/conversations fetch.
